items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I'm doing one album coming up that I'm going to be doing with Ray Bryant -- it's just a quartet album

ctx.x: etc. -- or arrangements for other bands, for which there are certain musical specifications. And I'm not sure if this question is gonna make much sense, but if you were gonna do something strictly for yourself and not have any kind of constraints; I mean, that is, you could use all the different kinds of instruments as you wanted, as many musicians or as few musicians as you liked, no time restraints, no financial restraints -- what would you do, or is this, maybe a silly question?

It is not a silly question. It's a very good question, Jim. It's a very good question particularly at this moment. Because I've just been talking about my next album or two that I'm going to do for Norman Granz for Pablo. And Norman has given me carte blanche do do anything I want to do. Now when I say "Anything" I want to do," you know, go and write or hire as many musicians as you want to, and this is probably for one or two albums.

Now the difficulty here with me is that it's a matter of making a decision. What do I want to do, you know? And you always feel like, gee, if I could only do just that what you really wanted to do, how would you go about it, what would you do? Of course, I'm doing one album coming up that I'm going to be doing with Ray Bryant -- it's just a quartet album, but then following that, I'll be doing an album with a big band, a number of men of my choice, the type of music of my choice, the composition of my choice --…
